item.title: Regulators close Indiana's United Fidelity Bank, the largest US bank failure since April 2024
item.description: The OCC closed United Fidelity Bank, a $5.9 billion lender based in Evansville, Indiana; First Citizens took over most deposits and assets, and the FDIC expects a $1.83 billion cost. (FDIC, FDIC Failed Bank List, Newsweek)

item.title: Wall Street closes its best week in more than a year as the S&P 500 gains 5.6%
item.description: The S&P 500 rose 1.6% on Friday and 5.6% over a holiday-shortened week, its best since April 2025, one week after falling into a correction. (KSL (AP), Global News (AP))

item.title: US goods trade deficit widens to $149.5 billion in October as AI equipment lifts imports to a record
item.description: The US goods deficit jumped 10.7% to $149.5 billion in October as imports reached a record $365.3 billion, led by capital goods tied to the AI buildout. (US Census Bureau, The Globe and Mail (Reuters))

item.title: Ottawa unveils a first national forestry strategy backed by $6.5 billion to move the industry beyond lumber and pulp
item.description: Canada's government set out a forestry strategy to 2050 with $6.5 billion for new plants, mill upgrades and wood supply, aiming to cut reliance on lumber, pulp and the US market. (The Globe and Mail, BNN Bloomberg (The Canadian Press))

item.title: SpaceX and Elon Musk pledge two shares to every active Trump Account, a gift valued at nearly $18 billion
item.description: SpaceX will issue one new share to every active Trump Account and Elon Musk will match it from his own holdings, a pledge worth nearly $18 billion at Wednesday's share price. (The Globe and Mail (Reuters), Fortune)

item.title: Beyond the First Best: Welfare and OPEC Market Power
item.description: A new framework for measuring cartel harm puts OPEC's cost to the world since 1970 at $2.2 trillion by the usual method, but about $0.7 trillion once other oil-market distortions are accounted for. (John Asker, Allan Collard-Wexler, Charlotte De Cannière et al.)

item.title: Euro zone countries pick Spain's Pablo Hernández de Cos to succeed Christine Lagarde as ECB president
item.description: Pablo Hernández de Cos, a former Bank of Spain governor, was chosen to lead the European Central Bank from February, with inflation at 4% and a December rate rise widely expected. (The Globe and Mail, CRBC News)

item.title: Chinese stocks post their biggest gains in two years after Beijing promises a larger role for state-backed buyers
item.description: The CSI 300 rose 4.2% and a chip index jumped a record 19% after China's cabinet said state-backed investors would do more to stabilise a market at 17-month lows. (Reuters (via WIFC), Oninvest)

item.title: Trump calls pre-election GDP figures "fake" and demands an investigation after a routine upward revision
item.description: President Trump alleged, without evidence, that officials deliberately understated third-quarter growth before the midterm elections, after a scheduled revision lifted it from 3.4% to 4.3%. (Fortune, Bloomberg (via The Spokesman-Review), Fox Business)

item.title: Fed's Beige Book finds slight to moderate growth in eight districts, with wage gains picking up and costs outpacing prices
item.description: The Federal Reserve's regional survey shows a slowly growing economy in which consumers are price sensitive, housing and construction are weakening and wage growth has stepped up to a moderate pace. (Federal Reserve, Federal Reserve)

item.title: AI, Automation, and Fiscal Pressure
item.description: A model calibrated to the EU finds that AI-driven automation can widen budget deficits even as it grows the economy, because income shifts from heavily taxed labor to lightly taxed capital. (Spencer Bastani, Georg Graetz, Bernat Pla et al.)

item.title: US proposes new Section 301 tariffs on China, the EU and 12 other trading partners over excess factory capacity
item.description: The Trump administration proposed new tariffs on 14 economies, including an additional 20% on Chinese goods, to replace import taxes the Supreme Court struck down in February. (The Globe and Mail, BBC, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: US PCE inflation holds at 3.8% in October and core inflation reaches 3.3%, as real consumer spending slips
item.description: The Federal Reserve's preferred price index rose 3.8% in the year to October, and 3.3% excluding food and energy, slightly above the 3.2% core rate economists expected. (Bureau of Economic Analysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: US third-quarter GDP growth is revised up to 4.3%, the fastest pace in three years
item.description: The US economy grew at a 4.3% annual rate in the third quarter, not 3.4% as first estimated, after upgrades to software investment and consumer spending. (Bureau of Economic Analysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Norse Atlantic suspends its flights and says it will file for bankruptcy unless it finds funding urgently
item.description: The Norwegian long-haul budget airline cancelled Thursday's flights a day after its shares fell 85%, and says it is in takeover talks with investors. (RTE, Euronews)

item.title: UK discount chain Poundland collapses into administration, putting 11,000 jobs and 600 shops at risk
item.description: Poundland's US owner, Gordon Brothers, put the retailer into administration after sale talks failed; shops stay open while administrators AlixPartners seek buyers for all or parts of it. (BBC, Euronews, BBC)

item.title: Democratizing Venture Capital: Tax Incentives and the Geographic Expansion of Startup Investing
item.description: Removing federal capital gains tax on qualifying startup stock in 2009–2010 raised the chance that a metro area with no venture capital received its first investment by 8 to 10 percentage points. (Murillo Campello, Guilherme Junqueira)

item.title: Britain's energy price cap will rise 26% in January, taking a typical annual bill to £2,166
item.description: Ofgem will lift the cap on default energy tariffs by 26% from 1 January after wholesale gas prices surged, affecting around 20 million households in England, Scotland and Wales. (Ofgem, BBC)

item.title: Bank of Canada will stress headline inflation and may raise rates sooner when supply shocks hit
item.description: Governor Tiff Macklem set out how the renewed 2% inflation framework will work in practice: more weight on headline CPI, new preferred core measures and a readiness to act early on large supply shocks. (Bank of Canada, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Dell's quarterly revenue doubles to $54.9 billion as its AI server backlog reaches $132 billion
item.description: Dell reported record third-quarter revenue of $54.9 billion, up 103%, raised its full-year revenue guidance to $202 billion and added $25 billion to its share buyback authorization. (Dell Technologies, BigGo Finance)

item.title: Subprime used-car dealer America's Car-Mart files for Chapter 11 and agrees to sell itself to a group led by former executives
item.description: America's Car-Mart filed a pre-packaged Chapter 11 case in Texas with $60 million of new financing and a deal to sell substantially all its assets to Cardinal Asset Holdings. (Yahoo Finance, Car Dealership Guy News)

item.title: CFOs Meet LLMs
item.description: An AI model asked to role-play individual chief financial officers predicted their actual survey answers on economic optimism, explaining 27% of the variation across 6,075 responses from 2002 to 2025. (John R. Graham, Campbell R. Harvey, Manish Jha · Duke University; NBER; Georgia State University)

item.title: Sanofi agrees to buy lung-disease drugmaker Insmed for about $41 billion in cash
item.description: Sanofi will pay $175 a share in cash for US drugmaker Insmed, a 46% premium, to add the fast-selling lung drug Brinsupri and reduce its reliance on Dupixent. (BioXconomy, Quartz)

item.title: New York Fed's Williams says inflation is too high and does not rule out rate increases at consecutive meetings
item.description: John Williams said restoring 2% inflation is "100 percent essential", expects inflation of about 3.5% this year, and told reporters that raising rates at back-to-back meetings remains possible. (Federal Reserve Bank of New York, The Jakarta Post (Reuters))

item.title: EU caps hybrid car imports from 1 December, limiting China to about 191,780 vehicles over 200 days
item.description: The European Commission has published temporary quotas on hybrid car imports from China, Japan, Turkey, South Korea, the UK and others, aimed mainly at a surge of Chinese hybrids. (The Guardian, electrive)

item.title: Best Buy raises its annual forecast after comparable sales grow 6.1%, its best quarter in five years
item.description: The electronics retailer beat its own expectations on computing, phones and new categories such as AI glasses, and lifted full-year sales and profit guidance ahead of the holidays. (Best Buy (Business Wire release), Rallies)

item.title: Five Facts About Stablecoins
item.description: Wallet-level blockchain data from 2020 to 2025 suggest dollar stablecoins are now used as money for payments rather than mainly for crypto speculation, with little sign that they drain bank deposits. (Lin William Cong, Gordon Y. Liao, Eswar S. Prasad et al. · Nanyang Technological University; Circle; Cornell University; Arizona State University)

item.title: CrowdStrike agrees to buy Zscaler in an all-stock deal worth about $43.9 billion
item.description: CrowdStrike will pay 1.135 of its shares for each Zscaler share, a 34% premium, to add network security to its device-security platform; its own shares fell more than 8% premarket. (Zscaler (joint press release), The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Taiwan eases margin-call rules as Asian authorities try to halt an AI-driven stock rout
item.description: After the Taiex lost 17.5% in a week, Taiwan cut the margin-maintenance threshold to 120% from 130%, tightened short-selling rules and kept its stabilization fund in the market; the index rebounded 2.16% on Monday. (Focus Taiwan (CNA), Focus Taiwan (CNA), The Globe and Mail (Reuters))

item.title: Trump threatens a "tremendous tax" on US companies that build AI data centres abroad
item.description: President Trump said US firms that build data centres overseas would face a heavy tax, but gave no details and said his staff were hearing the idea for the first time. (BBC, The Globe and Mail (AP))

item.title: A Missouri judge approves Bayer's $7.25 billion settlement of Roundup cancer claims
item.description: A St Louis state court found the deal "fair, reasonable and adequate", potentially ending most of the litigation that has weighed on Bayer since it bought Monsanto in 2018. (The Guardian, Insurance Journal)

item.title: Past Automation and Future AI: How Weak Links Tame the Growth Explosion
item.description: Jones and Tonetti find that automation explains essentially all US productivity growth since 1950, and that AI should speed growth up, but slowly, because tasks still done by people hold the economy back. (Charles I. Jones, Christopher Tonetti · Stanford GSB, Anthropic, NBER)

item.title: An AI sell-off pushes the S&P 500 and the Dow into a correction as Nvidia falls about 14%
item.description: The S&P 500 fell 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.28% on Friday, pushing the S&P 500 and Dow into a correction and erasing the Nasdaq's gains for the year as AI stocks slumped. (Fox Business, Yahoo Finance, Quartz)

item.title: The UK and EU agree deals on food trade, carbon markets and youth mobility, but tuition fees remain unresolved
item.description: The UK and EU agreed to ease Brexit checks on food, relink their emissions trading schemes and create a youth mobility scheme, in exchange for UK alignment with EU rules in those areas. (The Guardian, BBC)

item.title: Intuit agrees to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, less than a third of what it paid
item.description: Intuit will sell email marketing platform Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion, less than a third of the roughly $12 billion it paid in 2021, and use the cash to buy back shares. (Intuit, TechCrunch)

item.title: Canadian retail sales rise 0.8% in September on higher gas prices, but an early estimate points to a 1.5% drop in October
item.description: Canadian retail sales rose 0.8% to $75.3 billion in September, mostly on higher prices at gas stations, while sales volumes rose just 0.1% and an early estimate shows a 1.5% fall in October. (Statistics Canada, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Gambling for Goals
item.description: Using a survey linked to millions of Korean credit, telecom and card records, economists find that people who see life goals like homeownership as out of reach take more financial risks, such as trading crypto. (Costas Arkolakis, Spencer Y. Kwon, Dominic Russel et al.)

item.title: US retail sales rise just 0.2% in October as car purchases fall and prices outpace spending
item.description: US retail and food-service sales rose 0.2% in October to $748.2 billion, slowing from 0.8% in September, as auto dealers' sales fell and consumer prices rose faster than spending. (U.S. Census Bureau, StockAnalysis, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Walmart raises its annual outlook for the third time as US online sales grow 23%
item.description: Walmart's quarterly sales rose 5.2% to $188.8 billion and it raised its full-year guidance again, as shoppers across income groups seek lower prices and its online, marketplace and advertising businesses grow fast. (Walmart, The Globe and Mail)

item.title: Japan's core inflation rises to 2.2% in October, its fastest this year, as energy subsidies end
item.description: Japan's core consumer prices rose 2.2% from a year earlier in October, up from 2.1%, as expiring energy subsidies lifted power and gas bills, keeping a December Bank of Japan rate hike in view. (Xinhua, MLQ.ai, ActionForex)
